# CLI Reference

The `idea` binary is both the CLI and the daemon. Output is styled with [Charm.sh](https://charm.sh)
(Lip Gloss, Huh, Glamour, Bubble Tea) when stdout is a terminal, and falls back to plain text when it
is piped, redirected or scripted.

The table below is generated from the CLI's own command table — the same one `idea help` and the
dispatcher read. Run `make docs` after adding or renaming a command; `make docs-check` (and CI) fails
if this file has drifted.

## JSON output

The `--json` column above is the contract, per command:

- **`yes`** — the command prints its response as JSON on stdout and nothing else.
- **`takes no flags`** — `advance`, `execute`, `next` and `watch` accept positional arguments only.
  They are state-*changing* (or interactive), so a mistyped flag is an error rather than something
  they quietly treat as an initiative id.
- **`rejected`** — `plan` renders a markdown artifact, so there is no JSON form of it. It fails with
  a message pointing at `idea tasks --json` instead of ignoring the flag.
- **`—`** — the command has no JSON form. `prd` and `export` render markdown by design; the rest are
  actions whose output is a confirmation line.

Unknown flags are an error on every command that goes through the shared flag parser — the
`takes no flags` rows plus `tasks`, `changes`, `risk`, `explain`, `why`, `impact`, `trace`, `diff`
and `verify` — and on `new`, `docs add` and `executors setup`. The remaining commands still ignore
flags they do not recognize.

## Watching progress in real time

The daemon logs **every model request** (stage, role, model, duration) and every review cycle to
`~/.local/share/idea-harness/daemon.log`. To watch it live:

```bash
idea logs -f        # tail the log
# or run the daemon in the foreground in its own terminal:
idea daemon         # then run `idea new` in another terminal
```

The web UI shows a **Live activity** feed (same events, via SSE).

## How it works

The CLI is a thin HTTP client to the daemon (§29, D1). On the first state command it auto-starts a
detached daemon if none is running, then retries. The daemon is the single writer; the CLI never
mutates state directly.

Environment variables:

```text
IDEA_HARNESS_STATE   override the global state directory (default ~/.local/share/idea-harness)
IDEA_HARNESS_ADDR    override the daemon address (default 127.0.0.1:8787)
```

## Configuring providers

```bash
# List providers and their status (ready / missing key / not configured).
idea model

# Set the default model (provider/model).
idea model set gemini/gemini-2.5-flash

# Add a custom OpenAI-compatible provider.
idea model add groq --type openai --base-url https://api.groq.com/openai/v1 --key-env GROQ_API_KEY
```

Provider configuration is also available in the web UI under **Settings**.

## Example

```bash
mkdir my-product && cd my-product
idea init
idea model set ollama/llama3.1      # point at a local model
idea new                            # interactive Huh form
idea watch                          # follow the run live
idea prd                            # read the reviewed PRD in your terminal
```

The workflow runs asynchronously (Operations); `idea new` returns an operation id immediately, and
`idea watch` follows it to completion.
